title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene (182810) on chromosome 9q34.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous SPTAN1 mutations in dominant HMN families; HMND11 designation is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene is located on chromosome 9q34.

checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene; not itself in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Distal hereditary motor neuropathies are a rare subgroup of inherited peripheral neuropathies. They are marked by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant sensory involvement (Beijer et al., 2019). HMND11 is a form with juvenile onset, and disease severity varies greatly between patients.

paragraphs.text: Using next-generation sequencing, Beijer et al. (2019) identified heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene in affected members of 3 unrelated families with autosomal dominant juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy. Penetrance of the mutations was variable in 2 of the 3 families. Mutant SPTAN1 mRNA was degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, which reduced alpha-II spectrin protein levels in patient cells.

paragraphs.text: Beijer et al. (2019) found that mutant SPTAN1 mRNA carrying the nonsense mutations was degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, which reduced alpha-II spectrin protein levels in patient cells. This finding pointed to haploinsufficiency as the disease mechanism, in contrast to the dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations previously reported in epilepsy phenotypes.

checks.claim: SPTAN1 mutations previously reported in epilepsy phenotypes act by a dominant-negative mechanism, in contrast to the haploinsufficiency of SPTAN1 nonsense mutations in distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Previously, dominant-negative αII-spectrin gene mutations were described as causal in a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.
